recipes.name: Black Bean and Sweet Potato Chili
recipes.summary: A hearty meatless chili with sweet potatoes, two kinds of peppers, black beans and corn.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, poblano and jalapeño and cook, stirring now and then, until soft, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano and salt and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the sweet potatoes, beans, tomatoes with their juice and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Stir in the corn and simmer 5 minutes more. If you like it thicker, mash a few sweet potato cubes against the side of the pot.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt. Serve with your choice of toppings.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate up to 4 days. The chili thickens as it sits; add a splash of broth when reheating to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cool, then freeze in meal-size containers for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon over rice or baked potatoes, or roll into burritos with cheese; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Leave out the jalapeño for a mild pot and set out hot sauce for grown-ups. Kids like crushing tortilla chips on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream or use a dairy-free one.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole pot; portion some for lunches and freeze the rest.

recipes.name: Sweet Potato and Kale Hash with Eggs
recipes.summary: Crispy sweet potato cubes, peppers and kale in one skillet, topped with eggs.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potatoes in an even layer, cover and cook 8 minutes, stirring once, until they start to soften.
Uncover, add the onion, bell pepper, paprika, salt and pepper and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are tender and browned in spots.
Stir in the garlic and kale and cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the kale wilts.
Make 4 wells in the hash and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook over medium-low heat 5 to 7 minutes, until the whites and yolks are firm (160°F).
Season the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper and serve from the skillet.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the hash (without eggs) up to 4 days ahead. Reheat in a skillet until hot, then add the eggs.

freezer.text: The potatoes turn soft when frozen; keep the hash in the fridge instead.

leftovers.text: Fold leftover hash into a tortilla with cheese for a breakfast burrito; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can tear the kale leaves off the stems and crack the eggs into a small bowl first.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; brown 8 ounces of breakfast sausage first (to 160°F) for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Cube the sweet potatoes and chop the kale and peppers.

recipes.name: Maple-Roasted Sweet Potatoes and Brussels Sprouts
recipes.summary: A sheet-pan side of sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts with a light maple glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts with the oil, salt and pepper on a large baking sheet. Turn the sprouts cut side down and spread everything in one layer.
Roast 20 minutes, until the sprouts are browned underneath.
Drizzle with the maple syrup, add the pecans if using, and toss. Roast 8 to 10 minutes more, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the edges caramelize.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables up to 2 days ahead. Roasted leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Roasted vegetables turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Toss cold leftovers into a grain bowl or salad, or warm in a skillet.

recipes.kids: Cut the sprouts into quarters for little ones; the smaller pieces get extra crispy.

prep_day.ahead: Cube the sweet potatoes and trim the sprouts.

recipes.name: Chickpea and Cauliflower Curry
recipes.summary: A mild coconut curry with cauliflower, sweet potato, chickpeas and spinach. Serve over rice.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin and salt and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the cauliflower, sweet potato, chickpeas, tomatoes with their juice, coconut milk and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until it wilts. Add the lime juice and taste for salt.
Serve over rice, with cilantro if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate up to 4 days; the flavor deepens overnight. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the curry (without rice) for 2 to 3 months for best quality. The cauliflower softens a little.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch, or warm and spoon into a pita; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Curry powder is mild, not spicy. Start with 1 tablespoon for picky eaters and serve with plain yogurt.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the curry powder and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add 1 pound cubed chicken thighs with the onion and cook to 165°F for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the cauliflower and sweet potato; cook the curry and the rice.

recipes.name: Cheesy Stuffed Poblano Peppers
recipes.summary: Mild poblano halves filled with rice, black beans, corn and melted cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Bring the rice, water and a pinch of salt to a boil in a saucepan, cover, lower the heat and simmer 15 to 18 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile, rub the pepper halves with half the oil and set them cut side up in the baking dish. Bake 10 minutes, until they start to soften.
Heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, corn, tomatoes with their juice, salt and cooked rice. Simmer 3 minutes, until most of the liquid is gone. Stir in 1/2 cup of the cheese.
Pack the filling into the pepper halves and top with the rest of the cheese. Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the cheese is bubbling.
recipes.make_ahead: Fill the peppers up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate. Add 5 to 10 minutes to the baking time.

freezer.text: Freeze baked peppers for up to 2 months for best quality. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat covered until 165°F in the center, or chop and fold into a quesadilla.

recipes.kids: Poblanos are mild, but taste a strip first; some are hotter than others. Kids can sprinkle the cheese.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder label.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free shredded cheese.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; brown 1/2 pound ground beef to 160°F and add to the filling for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and make the filling.

recipes.name: Calabacitas (Squash, Corn and Green Chiles)
recipes.summary: A Southwest skillet side of zucchini, yellow squash, corn and mild green chiles.
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the zucchini and yellow squash and cook 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they start to soften.
Stir in the corn, green chiles, tomato, cumin and salt. Cook 4 to 5 minutes more, until the squash is tender but not mushy.
Sprinkle with cheese if you like, cover for 1 minute to melt, and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a skillet.

freezer.text: The squash turns watery when frozen.

leftovers.text: Fill tacos or quesadillas, or stir into scrambled eggs.

recipes.kids: Canned green chiles are mild. Kids can measure the corn and stir.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter and skip the cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the squash and onion.

recipes.name: Green Chile Cheese Egg Bake
recipes.summary: A chile relleno-style casserole of mild green chiles, two cheeses and eggs. Good for brunch or dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter the baking dish.
Spread half the chiles in the dish and top with half of each cheese. Repeat with the rest of the chiles and cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, salt and cumin until smooth, and pour over the chiles and cheese.
Bake 38 to 42 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the center (160°F).
Let it rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Serve with salsa if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate; add about 10 minutes to the baking time. Baked leftovers keep 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze baked squares, wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Warm a square and tuck it into a tortilla; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can layer the chiles and cheese and whisk the eggs.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 2 tablespoons cornstarch instead of the flour.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the whole pan for weekday breakfasts.

recipes.name: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos with Avocado Crema
recipes.summary: Spiced roasted cauliflower and poblano strips in corn tortillas with a crunchy lime slaw.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.

Toss the cauliflower and poblano with the oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt on the baking sheet. Spread in one layer and roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until tender and browned at the edges.
While it roasts, toss the cabbage with 2 tablespoons lime juice and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Blend or mash the avocado with the sour cream, 1 tablespoon lime juice and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave. Fill with cauliflower, slaw and crema.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the slaw up to 1 day ahead. The crema keeps 1 day pressed under plastic wrap so it stays green.

freezer.text: Roasted cauliflower turns soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat the cauliflower in a hot oven or skillet and serve over rice as a bowl.

recipes.kids: Set everything out taco-bar style so kids build their own. Leave the poblano strips on the side for anyone who wants it milder.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream and blend the avocado with 2 tablespoons water and the lime juice.
swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are usually gluten-free; check the label.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the cauliflower and make the slaw.

recipes.name: White Bean and Kale Soup
recipes.summary: An Italian-style pot of white beans, vegetables and kale in a tomato broth.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, Italian seasoning and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, broth and beans. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes.
For a thicker soup, mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot. Stir in the kale and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until tender.
Season with the salt and pepper, then taste. Serve with Parmesan if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F, adding a little water if it has thickened.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch in a preheated insulated food jar with a piece of crusty bread.

recipes.kids: Kids can strip the kale leaves from the stems and tear them into small pieces.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; brown 1/2 pound Italian sausage (to 160°F) before the vegetables for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables and kale; cook the soup.

recipes.name: Creamy Sausage, Potato and Kale Soup
recipes.summary: Italian sausage, sliced potatoes and kale in a lightly creamy broth.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Cook the sausage in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains (160°F), about 8 minutes. Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, then add the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth and add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the kale and cook 4 minutes, until wilted. Stir in the cream and heat through without boiling.
Taste and add salt and pepper; sausage and broth are already salty, so taste first.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat gently to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cream soups with potatoes turn grainy when frozen. Freeze the soup before adding the cream if you want to save some.

leftovers.text: Pack hot soup for lunch in a preheated insulated food jar.

recipes.kids: Use mild sausage and leave out the pepper flakes. Kids can tear the kale.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Use full-fat coconut milk in place of the cream.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, use vegetable broth and add a can of white beans plus 1 teaspoon fennel seed.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the potatoes (keep them covered in water in the fridge) and chop the kale.

recipes.name: Kale Salad with Apples and Cranberries
recipes.summary: Tender massaged kale with crisp apple, dried cranberries and sunflower seeds in a honey-lemon dressing.
steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until blended.
Put the kale in a large bowl, pour on half the dressing and squeeze and rub the leaves with clean hands for 2 to 3 minutes, until darker and softer.
Add the apple, cranberries, sunflower seeds and Parmesan if using. Toss with the rest of the dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: Massaged kale holds up well: dress it up to 1 day ahead and add the apple and seeds just before serving. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Pack in a lunchbox with an ice pack, or tuck into a wrap with turkey.

recipes.kids: Massaging the kale is a great kid job; it feels a little like squishing play dough.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and slice the kale; make the dressing.

recipes.name: Parmesan Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.summary: Cauliflower roasted until nutty and golden, with a crisp Parmesan finish.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the cauliflower with the oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper on a baking sheet and spread in one layer.
Roast 20 minutes, stirring once, until browned underneath.
Sprinkle with the Parmesan and roast 5 to 8 minutes more, until the cheese is golden.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the florets up to 3 days ahead. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Roasted cauliflower turns soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Chop into pasta with olive oil, or warm in a skillet and add to scrambled eggs.

recipes.kids: Call them cheesy trees. Small florets get the crispiest edges.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan and add 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the florets.

recipes.name: Cauliflower Fried Rice
recipes.summary: Riced cauliflower stir-fried with eggs, peas, carrot and green onions in about 20 minutes.
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggs and scramble until no liquid egg remains (160°F). Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the carrot and the green onion whites and cook 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the cauliflower rice straight from the freezer and the peas. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until hot and most of the moisture has cooked off.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, eggs and green onion greens. Serve hot.
recipes.make_ahead: Chop the vegetables up to 2 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Already-cooked cauliflower rice turns watery when frozen again.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch and reheat to 165°F; add leftover chicken or shrimp.

recipes.kids: Kids can crack and beat the eggs and measure the peas.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add diced cooked chicken with the soy sauce for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the carrot and green onions.

recipes.name: Broccoli Cauliflower Cheese Soup
recipes.summary: A creamy cheddar soup thick with broccoli and cauliflower florets.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, until smooth.
Add the broccoli, cauliflower, mustard, salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer (do not boil hard) and cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until the vegetables are tender.
For a smoother soup, mash or blend part of it. Turn the heat to low and stir in the cheese a handful at a time until melted. Taste for salt.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat gently over low heat, stirring, to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cheese soups can turn grainy when frozen.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in a preheated insulated food jar, or spoon over a baked potato.

recipes.kids: Kids can break the florets into small pieces and stir in the cheese.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into the cold milk instead of the flour.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the florets and shred the cheese.

recipes.name: Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts
recipes.summary: Crispy, deeply browned Brussels sprouts with a sweet-tart balsamic glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the sprouts with the oil, salt and pepper on the baking sheet. Turn them cut side down in one layer.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, without stirring, until the cut sides are deep brown and a knife slides in easily.
Stir the vinegar and honey together, drizzle over the hot sprouts and toss.
recipes.make_ahead: Trim and halve the sprouts up to 3 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Roasted sprouts turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat in a hot oven or skillet so they crisp again; chop into a grain bowl.

recipes.kids: The browned leaves that fall off are like chips. Let kids have the crispiest ones.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; toss with 4 strips of crumbled cooked bacon for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Trim and halve the sprouts.

recipes.name: Shaved Brussels Sprouts Salad
recipes.summary: Thinly sliced raw Brussels sprouts with toasted almonds, Parmesan and dried cranberries in a lemon dressing.
equipment: sharp knife or food processor with slicing blade
steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until blended.
Toast the almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Let cool.
Toss the sliced sprouts with the dressing and let stand 10 minutes so they soften a little.
Add the Parmesan, cranberries and almonds and toss again.
recipes.make_ahead: Dress the sprouts up to 1 day ahead; they stay crisp. Add the almonds just before serving. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Pile into a wrap with sliced turkey or chicken for lunch.

recipes.kids: Grown-ups slice the sprouts; kids can shake the dressing jar and sprinkle the toppings.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.nut_free: Use toasted sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the sprouts and make the dressing.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken with Brussels Sprouts and Butternut Squash
recipes.summary: Seasoned chicken thighs roasted on one pan with butternut squash, Brussels sprouts and red onion.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir the oil and seasonings together in a large bowl.
Toss the squash, sprouts and onion in the bowl with about two-thirds of the seasoned oil and spread on the baking sheet. Roast 10 minutes.
Toss the chicken in the rest of the seasoned oil. Push the vegetables to the edges and lay the chicken in the middle. Wash your hands and anything that touched the raw chicken.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes more, stirring the vegetables once, until the squash is tender and the thickest piece of chicken reads 165°F.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables up to 2 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: The roasted vegetables turn soft when frozen; cooked chicken alone freezes well for 2 to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Slice the chicken over salad greens with the vegetables, or wrap it all in a tortilla; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can toss the vegetables in the bowl (before the raw chicken comes out).

swaps.gluten_free: Already gluten-free; check the spice labels.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained chickpeas instead of the chicken and add them for the last 15 minutes.

prep_day.ahead: Cube the squash and halve the sprouts.

recipes.name: Harvest Quinoa Bowls
recipes.summary: Roasted butternut squash and Brussels sprouts over quinoa and kale with chickpeas, feta and pecans.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the squash, sprouts and chickpeas with the oil, salt and cumin on the baking sheet. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until the squash is tender and browned.
Meanwhile, bring the quinoa and water to a boil with a pinch of salt. Cover, lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar. Toss the kale with 2 tablespoons of dressing and rub it with your hands for a minute to soften.
Divide the quinoa and kale among 4 bowls. Top with the roasted vegetables, chickpeas, feta and pecans, and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: Roast the vegetables and cook the quinoa up to 4 days ahead. Pack bowls with the dressing on the side.

freezer.text: Cooked quinoa freezes well for 2 months, but the roasted vegetables and kale do not.

leftovers.text: Eat cold from the fridge, or warm the quinoa and vegetables before adding the kale.

recipes.kids: Set out the parts separately so kids can build their own bowls.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta or use avocado.
swaps.nut_free: Use pumpkin seeds instead of pecans.

prep_day.ahead: Roast the vegetables, cook the quinoa and make the dressing; pack 4 lunches.

recipes.name: Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.summary: A smooth, gently spiced squash soup with carrot and onion. A touch of cream is optional.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

ingredients.prep: peeled, seeded and cut in 1-inch cubes (about 8 cups)

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the squash, apple, broth, salt, nutmeg and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until the squash is very tender.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. If using a countertop blender, let the soup cool 5 minutes, fill the jar no more than half full, and hold the lid down with a towel.
Stir in the cream if using and taste for salt. Top with pumpkin seeds if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze before adding cream for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in a preheated insulated food jar with a grilled cheese sandwich.

recipes.kids: Microwave the whole squash 3 minutes to make peeling easier for the grown-up. Kids can measure and stir.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter and coconut milk instead of cream.
swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.

prep_day.ahead: Peel and cube the squash; cook a batch of soup.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Roasted Acorn Squash
recipes.summary: Acorn squash halves baked with butter, brown sugar and a pinch of cinnamon until spoon-tender.
equipment: rimmed baking sheet or baking dish

ingredients.prep: halved through the stem and seeded

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. To halve the squash safely, set it on a damp towel so it does not roll and cut with a large knife.
Score the flesh in a crisscross pattern without cutting through the skin. Set the halves cut side up on the pan.
Spread the butter in the halves and sprinkle with the brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Bake 45 to 55 minutes, until a knife slides in easily and the tops are glazed. Spoon the buttery syrup over the flesh before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 3 days ahead and reheat in the oven or microwave.

freezer.text: Scoop the cooked flesh, mash and freeze up to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Mash the flesh and stir into oatmeal, or spread on toast with a little salt.

recipes.kids: Kids can scoop out the seeds with a spoon and sprinkle the sugar.

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut oil or olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the squash halves.

recipes.name: Baked Spaghetti Squash Marinara
recipes.summary: Roasted spaghetti squash strands baked in marinara under melted mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rub the cut sides of the squash with the oil and salt and set cut side down on the baking sheet.
Roast 35 to 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Let cool 10 minutes, then scrape the flesh into strands with a fork.
Spread a little marinara in the baking dish. Toss the squash strands with the rest of the sauce and the Italian seasoning and spread in the dish.
Top with the mozzarella and Parmesan. Bake 15 minutes, until bubbling and the cheese melts.
recipes.make_ahead: Roast and shred the squash up to 3 days ahead. Assemble and refrigerate up to 1 day before baking; add 10 minutes and heat until 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Spaghetti squash turns watery when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat covered until 165°F in the center.

recipes.kids: Scraping the strands with a fork is a fun reveal; let kids do it once the squash has cooled.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheeses and top with breadcrumbs toasted in olive oil.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; stir in 1 pound browned ground beef or turkey (to 160°F or 165°F) for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Roast and shred the squash.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Bread
recipes.summary: A moist, spiced quick bread made with canned pumpkin. One bowl, no mixer.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pan.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and pumpkin pie spice in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the pumpkin, both sugars, oil, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the flour mixture just until no dry streaks remain.
Pour into the pan and bake 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack. Let it cool at least 10 more minutes before slicing.
recipes.make_ahead: Wrap and keep at room temperature up to 2 days or in the fridge up to 1 week.

freezer.text: Freeze the whole loaf or slices, wrapped well, for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.

leftovers.text: Toast a slice and spread with cream cheese or butter.

recipes.kids: Kids can whisk the dry ingredients and scrape the pumpkin out of the can.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: It is already dairy-free.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a loaf for breakfasts and snacks.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Spice Pancakes
recipes.summary: Fluffy fall pancakes with canned pumpkin and warm spices.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spice in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, pumpkin, egg, melted butter and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; small lumps are fine. Let rest 5 minutes.

Heat a griddle over medium heat and brush with butter. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and the edges look dry, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until cooked through in the center.
Keep warm on a baking sheet in a 200°F oven while you cook the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the dry ingredients in a jar the night before. Cooked pancakes keep 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled pancakes in one layer, then bag for up to 2 months for best quality. Reheat in the toaster.

leftovers.text: Toast a cold pancake and spread with peanut butter for a snack.

recipes.kids: Pumpkin batter is thick, so pancakes cook a little slower. Kids can whisk and pour with help.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil instead of butter.
swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a double batch and freeze for weekdays.

recipes.name: Classic Pumpkin Pie
recipes.summary: A smooth, spiced pumpkin custard in a flaky crust, the way it is served at Thanksgiving.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Fit the crust into the pie plate and crimp the edge. Set the plate on a baking sheet.
Whisk the pumpkin, evaporated milk, eggs, sugar, salt and spices until smooth. Pour into the crust.
Bake 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 350°F and bake 40 to 50 minutes more, until the edges are set, the center jiggles only slightly and a knife near the center comes out clean (at least 160°F).
Cool on a rack about 2 hours, then refrigerate. The filling finishes setting as it cools.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 2 days ahead. Pumpkin pie is an egg custard, so keep it in the fridge, covered, once cool and up to 3 to 4 days.

freezer.text: Freeze the baked, cooled pie, wrapped well, for up to 1 month. Thaw overnight in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Keep slices refrigerated and enjoy cold or at room temperature within 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can whisk the filling and help crimp the crust. If a crust edge browns fast, a grown-up can cover it with foil strips.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free pie crust.
swaps.dairy_free: Use full-fat coconut milk instead of evaporated milk and skip the whipped cream.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the pie a day or two before you need it.

recipes.name: Turkey Pumpkin Chili
recipes.summary: Ground turkey and two kinds of beans in a thick tomato and pumpkin base with mild chili spices.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the turkey, onion and bell pepper and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 165°F, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, cinnamon and salt and cook 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin, tomatoes with their juice, beans and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Taste for salt and serve with cheese and sour cream if you like.
Slow cooker: brown the turkey and vegetables first (steps 1 and 2), then put everything in the cooker and cook on low 6 hours.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cool, then freeze in meal-size containers for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon over baked sweet potatoes or rice; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: The pumpkin makes it mild and a little sweet. Kids can open and rinse the beans with a grown-up.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Skip the turkey, use vegetable broth and add a third can of beans.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole pot; portion for lunches and freeze the rest.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Baked Oatmeal
recipes.summary: A sliceable pan of oats baked with pumpkin, milk and maple. Make it once for a week of breakfasts.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Butter the baking dish.
Stir the oats, baking powder, spice and salt together in a large bowl.
Whisk the pumpkin, milk, eggs, maple syrup, melted butter and vanilla in another bowl. Pour over the oats and stir well. Spread in the dish and sprinkle with pecans if using.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the center is set and no longer wet and the edges are golden. Let cool 5 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Warm squares in the microwave with a splash of milk.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled squares, wrapped, for up to 3 months. Microwave from frozen.

leftovers.text: Eat cold from a lunchbox or warm with a spoonful of yogurt.

recipes.kids: Kids can measure the oats and stir everything together.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and coconut oil.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the pan for weekday breakfasts.

recipes.name: Mushroom Barley Soup
recipes.summary: A rich, old-fashioned soup of browned mushrooms, vegetables and chewy pearl barley.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and cook until browned and their liquid has cooked off, about 8 minutes total.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the barley, broth, soy sauce and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 40 to 45 minutes, until the barley is tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Season with the salt and pepper and taste.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge. The barley soaks up broth, so add water when reheating to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch in a preheated insulated food jar.

recipes.kids: Kids can wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp paper towel and slice them with a butter knife.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; use beef broth and add 1 pound browned stew beef for a meat version (simmer until tender).

prep_day.ahead: Slice the mushrooms and chop the vegetables; cook the soup.

recipes.name: Mushroom and Asparagus Risotto
recipes.summary: Creamy stovetop risotto with browned mushrooms, asparagus, peas and Parmesan.
equipment: large heavy saucepan or Dutch oven
steps: Warm the broth in a saucepan over low heat.
Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter with the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms until browned, about 6 minutes. Lift them out onto a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the shallot and garlic 2 minutes, then add the rice and stir 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges look clear.
Add a ladle of warm broth and stir until it is mostly absorbed. Keep adding broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, for about 18 minutes.

Stir in the asparagus with another ladle of broth and cook 5 to 6 minutes more, until the rice is creamy and just tender and the asparagus is bright green. Stir in the peas and mushrooms to heat through.
Off the heat, stir in the Parmesan, the rest of the butter and the lemon juice. Season and serve right away; risotto thickens as it stands.
recipes.make_ahead: Prep the vegetables up to 2 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of broth to 165°F.

freezer.text: Risotto turns grainy when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat with broth, or shape cold risotto into patties and pan-fry until hot in the center (165°F).

recipes.kids: Older kids can take turns stirring with a grown-up nearby; the pan stays hot.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter and skip the Parmesan; add 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast if you have it.

prep_day.ahead: Trim the asparagus and slice the mushrooms.

recipes.name: Tofu, Mushroom and Bok Choy Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: Crisp tofu cubes, mushrooms and bok choy in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce.
equipment: clean kitchen towel or paper towels

ingredients.prep: extra-firm, pressed and cut in 3/4-inch cubes
cut in 1-inch pieces, stems and leaves separated

steps: Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.

Toss the tofu cubes with 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu, turning now and then, until golden on most sides, 8 to 10 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the mushrooms and cook 4 minutes, until browned. Add the bok choy stems and cook 2 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and bok choy leaves and cook 1 minute, until the leaves wilt.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and cook 1 minute, until glossy. Return the tofu and toss. Serve over rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Press and cube the tofu and mix the sauce up to 2 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Bok choy turns limp when frozen.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch and reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can press the tofu between towels under a heavy book and stir the sauce.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; use 1 pound sliced chicken breast instead of tofu, cooked to 165°F, for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Press the tofu, cut the vegetables and mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Spring Vegetable Frittata
recipes.summary: A thick oven-finished omelet with asparagus, mushrooms, spinach and feta.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms 5 minutes, until browned. Add the asparagus and green onions and cook 3 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Spread the vegetables evenly and pour in the eggs. Sprinkle with the feta. Cook without stirring 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges start to set.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake 12 to 15 minutes, until puffed and set in the center (160°F). Use an oven mitt; the handle is hot.
Let stand 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.
recipes.make_ahead: Refrigerate wedges up to 4 days. Eat cold, or microwave until hot (165°F).

freezer.text: Frittata with this many vegetables turns watery when frozen.

leftovers.text: Tuck a cold wedge into a pita for lunch.

recipes.kids: Kids can crack the eggs into a separate bowl first (so shells are easy to fish out) and whisk.

swaps.dairy_free: Use water instead of milk and skip the feta.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the frittata for grab-and-go breakfasts.

recipes.name: Lemon Parmesan Roasted Asparagus
recipes.summary: Asparagus roasted in 10 minutes with garlic, lemon and a little Parmesan.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the asparagus with the oil, garlic, salt and pepper on the baking sheet and spread in one layer.
Roast 8 to 12 minutes, depending on thickness, until tender-crisp.
Sprinkle with the Parmesan and lemon juice while hot.
recipes.make_ahead: Trim the asparagus up to 2 days ahead and store standing in a jar with an inch of water. Leftovers keep 3 days.

freezer.text: Cooked asparagus turns limp when frozen.

leftovers.text: Chop into scrambled eggs, pasta or a grain bowl.

recipes.kids: Show kids how a spear snaps on its own where the tough part ends.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.

prep_day.ahead: Trim the asparagus.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Lemon Garlic Salmon and Asparagus
recipes.summary: Salmon fillets and asparagus roasted together on one pan with lemon and garlic, in about 25 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir the oil, garlic, lemon juice, dill, salt and pepper together.
Spread the asparagus on one side of the baking sheet and toss with about a third of the lemon-garlic oil.
Set the salmon skin side down on the other side and brush with the rest. Lay lemon slices on top if using.
Roast 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and reads 145°F in the thickest part.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the lemon-garlic oil and trim the asparagus up to 1 day ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Cooked salmon dries out when frozen and reheated.

leftovers.text: Flake cold salmon over a salad or into a wrap, or reheat gently to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Check small portions for pin bones before serving to little ones.

swaps.gluten_free: Already gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Already dairy-free.

prep_day.ahead: Trim the asparagus and mix the lemon-garlic oil.

recipes.name: Pasta Primavera
recipes.summary: Penne tossed with sautéed spring vegetables, garlic, lemon and Parmesan.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the penne by the package directions. Before draining, scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the asparagus, zucchini and bell pepper 5 to 6 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Add the garlic, tomatoes and peas and cook 2 minutes. Season with 3/4 teaspoon salt and the pepper.
Toss the drained pasta with the vegetables, Parmesan, lemon juice and enough pasta water to make a light, glossy sauce. Top with basil if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables up to 2 days ahead. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: The vegetables turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Eat cold as a pasta salad with a splash of Italian dressing, or reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can snap the asparagus and halve cherry tomatoes with a butter knife.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free penne.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan and add more olive oil and lemon.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add sliced cooked chicken for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables.

recipes.name: Skillet Ratatouille
recipes.summary: A French summer stew of eggplant, zucchini, peppers and tomatoes, simmered until soft and rich.
equipment: large deep skillet or Dutch oven
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, until browned and softened, about 8 minutes. Move to a bowl.
Add the rest of the oil, the onion and peppers and cook 5 minutes. Add the zucchini and cook 4 minutes more. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Return the eggplant to the pan with the tomatoes, thyme, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover partly and cook 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until everything is very tender.
Taste for salt and top with basil if you like. Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.make_ahead: Ratatouille tastes better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat or serve at room temperature.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months for best quality. The vegetables soften a little more.

leftovers.text: Spoon over pasta or polenta, top with a fried egg, or fill an omelet.

recipes.kids: Cut the vegetables small for little ones, and serve it over pasta with Parmesan.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; serve beside roast chicken or sausages for a meat meal.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables and cook the whole pan.

recipes.name: Zucchini Bread
recipes.summary: A moist cinnamon quick bread that uses up 2 cups of grated zucchini.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pan.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk both sugars, the oil, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the zucchini (no need to squeeze it).
Stir in the flour mixture just until no dry streaks remain, then fold in the walnuts if using.
Pour into the pan and bake 50 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.
recipes.make_ahead: Wrap and keep at room temperature up to 2 days or in the fridge up to 1 week.

freezer.text: Freeze the loaf or slices, wrapped well, for up to 3 months. Grated raw zucchini also freezes in 2-cup bags for the next loaf.

leftovers.text: Toast a slice and spread with cream cheese.

recipes.kids: Kids can grate the zucchini on the large holes with a grown-up watching their knuckles, and stir the batter.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: It is already dairy-free.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a loaf for breakfasts and snacks.

recipes.name: Baked Eggplant Parmesan
recipes.summary: Crisp oven-baked eggplant slices layered with marinara and mozzarella. No frying.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Brush the baking sheets with half the oil. Sprinkle the eggplant with the salt.
Beat the eggs with the water in a shallow bowl. Mix the panko, 1/2 cup Parmesan and Italian seasoning in another.
Dip each slice in egg, then press into the crumbs. Lay on the baking sheets and brush the tops with the rest of the oil.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, flipping once, until golden and tender. Lower the oven to 375°F.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish. Layer half the eggplant, 1 cup sauce and 1 cup mozzarella. Repeat, then sprinkle with the last 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Bake 25 minutes, until bubbling and 165°F in the center. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake the eggplant slices up to 2 days ahead. Assemble and refrigerate up to 1 day; add 10 to 15 minutes and check that the center reaches 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled, unbaked or baked, wrapped well, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and bake until 165°F in the center.

leftovers.text: Tuck a reheated square into a roll for an eggplant Parmesan sub; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can run the breading station: one hand for the egg, one for the crumbs.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free panko or crushed rice cereal.

prep_day.ahead: Bread and bake the eggplant; assemble the dish.

recipes.name: Baba Ganoush
recipes.summary: A smoky roasted eggplant dip with tahini, lemon and garlic. Serve with pita and vegetables.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Prick the eggplants all over with a fork and set on the baking sheet.
Roast 40 to 45 minutes, turning once, until collapsed and very soft. Let cool 15 minutes.
Split the eggplants and scoop the flesh into a strainer. Let it drain 5 minutes; discard the skins.
Mash the flesh with a fork (or pulse in a food processor) with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and cumin. Spread in a bowl and drizzle with the oil.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge, covered. The flavor gets smokier overnight.

freezer.text: The dip turns watery when frozen.

leftovers.text: Spread in a wrap with chicken or vegetables, or use as a sandwich spread.

recipes.kids: Kids can scoop the soft eggplant from the skins with a spoon once cool.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers instead of pita.

prep_day.ahead: Roast the eggplant and make the dip for lunchboxes.

recipes.name: Pasta alla Norma
recipes.summary: A Sicilian pasta with browned eggplant in garlicky tomato sauce, topped with ricotta and basil.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tablespoon salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant and 3/4 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring now and then, until browned on all sides and soft, 10 to 12 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute. Stir in the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, until thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta by the package directions. Save 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and most of the basil, adding pasta water if it seems dry. Serve topped with spoonfuls of ricotta, the rest of the basil and Parmesan if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the sauce up to 4 days ahead. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the sauce alone for up to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Reheat with a splash of water until 165°F; pack for lunch.

recipes.kids: The eggplant melts into the sauce, so it often passes for plain tomato pasta.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free penne.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the ricotta and Parmesan; finish with extra olive oil.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless.

prep_day.ahead: Make the sauce.

recipes.name: Garlic Eggplant Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: Silky eggplant in a sweet, savory garlic and ginger sauce, Chinese takeout style.
steps: Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant and cook, turning now and then, 5 minutes.
Add 1/4 cup water, cover and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the eggplant is very tender. Uncover and let any water cook off.
Push the eggplant aside, add the last tablespoon of oil, the garlic, ginger and green onion whites, and stir 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and toss until thick and glossy, 1 minute. Top with the green onion greens and serve over rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the sauce up to 4 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cooked eggplant turns mushy when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and spoon over rice or noodles.

recipes.kids: Kids can stir the sauce. The hoisin makes it a little sweet.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free hoisin.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; brown 1/2 pound ground pork (to 160°F) before the eggplant for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the eggplant and mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.summary: Beets, carrots, parsnips and sweet potato roasted with rosemary until sweet and caramelized.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the beets with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt and keep them at one end of the baking sheet so they do not stain everything pink.
Toss the other vegetables with the rest of the oil, the rosemary, salt and pepper and spread on the rest of the pan in one layer.
Roast 35 to 40 minutes, stirring once, until everything is tender and browned at the edges.
recipes.make_ahead: Peel and cut the vegetables up to 3 days ahead (keep the beets separate). Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Roasted root vegetables turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Toss with greens and goat cheese for a salad, or warm in a skillet with a fried egg.

recipes.kids: Wear an apron for beets; their juice stains. Kids can toss the vegetables with oil in a bowl.

prep_day.ahead: Peel and cut the vegetables.

recipes.name: Roasted Beet and Goat Cheese Salad
recipes.summary: Sweet roasted beets over peppery arugula with tangy goat cheese, toasted walnuts and a balsamic dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Wrap the beets in foil, set in a small baking dish and roast 50 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Let cool 20 minutes, then rub off the skins with a paper towel and cut the beets in wedges.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the arugula with half the dressing and spread on a platter. Top with the beets, goat cheese and walnuts and drizzle with the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Roast and peel the beets up to 5 days ahead and keep them covered in the fridge. Toss the salad just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze the salad.

leftovers.text: Pack beets, cheese and nuts in a container with the greens separate and dress at lunch.

recipes.kids: Some kids love bright pink beets; try a few wedges with a little goat cheese on the side.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the goat cheese and add avocado.
swaps.nut_free: Use toasted pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.

prep_day.ahead: Roast and peel the beets; make the dressing.

recipes.name: Pink Beet Hummus
recipes.summary: Classic hummus blended with roasted beet for a bright pink, slightly sweet dip.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Wrap the beets in foil and roast 50 to 60 minutes, until tender. Cool, rub off the skins and cut in chunks.
Blend the tahini and lemon juice 1 minute, until creamy.
Add the beets, chickpeas, garlic, oil, cumin and salt and blend until smooth, scraping down the sides. Add water a tablespoon at a time until it is as smooth as you like.
Taste for salt and lemon. Serve with vegetables or pita.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge, covered. Roasted beets keep 5 days too.

freezer.text: Freeze in small containers for up to 2 months. Stir well after thawing in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Spread in a wrap or on a sandwich, or pack with crackers for lunch.

recipes.kids: Kids love the color. Let them push the blender button with a grown-up holding the lid.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers.

prep_day.ahead: Roast the beets and blend the hummus for lunchboxes.

recipes.name: Vegetable Borscht
recipes.summary: An Eastern European beet soup with cabbage, potatoes and carrots, finished with a swirl of sour cream.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot 5 minutes. Add the beets and cook 5 minutes more, stirring.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the broth, potatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the vinegar, salt and pepper and taste. Serve with sour cream and dill if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Borscht is even better the next day. Keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality. The potatoes soften a little.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in a preheated insulated food jar with a slice of rye bread.

recipes.kids: Grate beets with gloves on or expect pink hands for a while. Kids can stir in their own sour cream swirl.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; use beef broth and add 1 pound stew beef simmered until tender for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Grate the beets and carrots and shred the cabbage; cook the soup.

recipes.name: Quick Pickled Beets
recipes.summary: Tender beets and red onion in a sweet-tangy brine. Fridge pickles, no canning.
steps: Cover the beets with water in a pot, bring to a boil and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain and cool until you can handle them, then slip off the skins and slice 1/4 inch thick.
Bring the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and cloves to a boil in a small saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Layer the beets and onion in the jar and pour the hot brine over them. Cool, then cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours before eating.
recipes.make_ahead: These are refrigerator pickles, not canned. Keep them covered in the fridge and eat within 2 weeks.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Slice onto salads, sandwiches and grain bowls.

recipes.kids: Kids can layer the cooled beet slices and onion in the jar.

prep_day.ahead: Cook and pickle the beets; they keep all week.

recipes.name: Creamy Cucumber Radish Salad
recipes.summary: Crisp cucumbers and radishes in a cool sour cream and dill dressing.
steps: Stir the sour cream, vinegar, sugar, dill, salt and pepper together in a large bowl.
Add the cucumbers, radishes and onion and toss to coat.
Serve right away, or chill up to 4 hours. Stir before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the vegetables up to 1 day ahead and keep them wrapped in a towel in the fridge. The dressed salad keeps 1 day but gets watery.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Spoon into a pita with chicken or falafel.

recipes.kids: Kids can slice cucumbers with a butter knife and stir the dressing.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt, or dress with 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons vinegar instead.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the cucumbers and radishes.

recipes.name: Butter Roasted Radishes
recipes.summary: Roasting turns radishes mild, juicy and a little sweet, a lot like new potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the radishes with the butter, salt and pepper on the baking sheet and turn them cut side down.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, until tender and browned on the cut sides.
Toss with the lemon juice and parsley if using.
recipes.make_ahead: Trim the radishes up to 3 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Roasted radishes turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Warm in a skillet and serve with eggs.

recipes.kids: Raw radishes can taste spicy; roasted ones are mild. Let kids taste one of each.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Trim the radishes.

recipes.name: Avocado Toast with Radishes and Eggs
recipes.summary: Mashed avocado on toasted sourdough with crisp sliced radishes and a fried egg.
steps: Mash the avocados with the lemon juice and half the salt.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs, cover and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the whites and yolks are firm (160°F). Sprinkle with the rest of the salt.
Meanwhile, toast the bread.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with radish slices and an egg, and add pepper flakes if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the radishes up to 2 days ahead and keep them in a container with a damp paper towel. Mash the avocado just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

recipes.kids: Kids can mash the avocado with a fork and arrange the radish slices in patterns.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.
swaps.dairy_free: Cook the eggs in olive oil.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the radishes.

recipes.name: Quick Pickled Radishes
recipes.summary: Bright pink, crunchy radish slices in a tangy brine for tacos, bowls and sandwiches.
steps: Pack the radishes, garlic and jalapeño if using into the jar.
Bring the vinegar, water, sugar and salt to a boil in a small saucepan, stirring until dissolved.
Pour the hot brine over the radishes. Cool, then cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour. They turn pink overnight.
recipes.make_ahead: These are refrigerator pickles, not canned. Keep them covered in the fridge and eat within 2 weeks; they soften over time.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Pile on tacos, burgers, grain bowls and avocado toast.

recipes.kids: Kids can pack the slices into the jar and watch them change color.

prep_day.ahead: Make a jar for the week.

recipes.name: Mexican Chopped Salad
recipes.summary: Romaine, black beans, corn, avocado, tomatoes and radishes in a lime-cumin dressing.
steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until blended.
Toss the romaine, beans, corn, tomatoes, radishes, onion and cilantro in a large bowl.
Add the avocado and dressing and toss gently. Top with crushed chips if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Chop everything but the avocado up to 1 day ahead and keep the dressing separate. Dice the avocado just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Fold into a tortilla with cheese, or pack with the dressing on the side.

recipes.kids: Kids can rinse the beans, measure the corn and shake the dressing.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; top with grilled chicken or shrimp for a main dish.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables and make the dressing.

recipes.name: Fresh Guacamole
recipes.summary: Chunky avocado dip with lime, onion, tomato, cilantro and a little jalapeño.
steps: Halve and pit the avocados and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Add the lime juice and salt and mash to the texture you like.
Stir in the onion, tomato, jalapeño and cilantro. Taste and add more salt or lime.
Serve right away, or press plastic wrap onto the surface and chill up to 4 hours.
recipes.make_ahead: Chop the onion, tomato and jalapeño up to 1 day ahead. Make the guacamole the day you eat it.

freezer.text: Plain mashed avocado with lime freezes for 2 to 3 months; add the fresh vegetables after thawing.

leftovers.text: Press plastic onto the surface and refrigerate up to 1 day. Scrape off any brown layer.

recipes.kids: Kids can mash the avocado. Leave out the jalapeño for a mild bowl.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the onion, tomato and jalapeño.

recipes.name: Cobb Salad
recipes.summary: A dinner-size salad with rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese.
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water by an inch and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 12 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Spread the romaine on a platter. Arrange the chicken, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in rows on top. Drizzle with dressing at the table.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the eggs and bacon and make the dressing up to 3 days ahead. Dice the avocado when serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Pack the toppings and greens separately with the dressing on the side; eat within 1 day.

recipes.kids: Serve the rows separately as a build-your-own plate. Swap mild cheddar for the blue cheese.

swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the blue cheese.
swaps.gluten_free: Check the rotisserie chicken and bacon labels.

prep_day.ahead: Hard-cook the eggs, cook the bacon and make the dressing.

recipes.name: Southern Collard Greens
recipes.summary: Collards simmered low and slow with bacon, onion and a splash of vinegar until silky.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
large bowl or clean sink for washing greens

ingredients.prep: stems removed, leaves cut in 1-inch ribbons

steps: Wash the collards well in a sink of cold water, lifting them out so the grit stays behind. Repeat if you see sand.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, about 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the collards a few handfuls at a time, stirring until they wilt enough to fit. Add the broth, vinegar and brown sugar.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring now and then, until very tender.
Taste and add the salt (the bacon and broth are salty, so taste first). Serve with some of the cooking liquid.
recipes.make_ahead: Collards taste even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze greens with some of their liquid for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Stir into rice and beans, or serve with cornbread and the cooking liquid.

recipes.kids: Kids can tear the leaves off the stems and swish them in the washing water.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the bacon and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the bacon, cook the onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil with 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and use vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and cut the collards; cook the whole pot.

recipes.name: Garlicky Sautéed Swiss Chard
recipes.summary: Swiss chard stems and leaves cooked quickly in olive oil with garlic and lemon.

ingredients.prep: stems sliced, leaves chopped, kept separate

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chard stems and cook 4 minutes, until starting to soften.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute, until the garlic is golden at the edges.
Add the chard leaves (with any water still clinging to them) and the salt. Cover and cook 2 minutes, then uncover and toss until wilted and tender, 2 to 3 minutes more.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Wash and cut the chard up to 3 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Sautéed chard turns watery when frozen.

leftovers.text: Fold into an omelet or quesadilla, or toss with pasta and Parmesan.

recipes.kids: Rainbow chard has red, yellow and pink stems. Let kids pick a bunch at the store.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and cut the chard.

recipes.name: Caldo Verde (Potato, Greens and Sausage Soup)
recipes.summary: A Portuguese soup of creamy blended potatoes, thin ribbons of collard greens and smoked sausage.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

ingredients.prep: stems removed, leaves rolled and sliced in very thin ribbons

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the sausage 5 minutes and lift it out onto a plate.
Cook the onion in the same pot 5 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart when poked.
Mash or blend the potatoes right in the pot until the broth is creamy, leaving some chunks if you like.
Stir in the collards and sausage and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until the greens are tender and the soup is steaming hot (165°F). Season with the salt and pepper and taste.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F, adding a little broth if it has thickened.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 2 months for best quality. Stir well when reheating.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in a preheated insulated food jar with crusty bread.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the collard leaves up like cigars for a grown-up to slice.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika with the garlic and use vegetable broth plus a can of white beans.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the potatoes (keep covered in water in the fridge) and slice the greens.

recipes.name: Sausage, White Bean and Chard Pasta
recipes.summary: Penne tossed with browned Italian sausage, white beans, wilted chard, garlic and Parmesan.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the penne by the package directions; save 1/2 cup of the water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains (160°F), about 8 minutes.
Add the chard stems and cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the chard leaves, beans and broth and simmer 4 to 5 minutes, until the leaves are tender.
Toss in the pasta and Parmesan, adding pasta water as needed for a light sauce.
recipes.make_ahead: Wash and cut the chard up to 3 days ahead. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: The pasta and greens turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat with a splash of broth until 165°F; pack for lunch.

recipes.kids: Use mild sausage and chop the chard leaves small so they blend in.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free penne and check the sausage label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, use vegetable broth and add a second can of beans.

prep_day.ahead: Wash and cut the chard.

recipes.name: Chard and Ricotta Lasagna Roll-Ups
recipes.summary: Lasagna noodles rolled around a cheesy ricotta and Swiss chard filling, baked in marinara.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the noodles in boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain and lay flat on oiled foil so they do not stick.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the chard and garlic 4 to 5 minutes, until wilted and the liquid cooks off. Let cool a few minutes.
Stir the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, Parmesan, egg, Italian seasoning, salt and cooled chard together.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish. Spread about 1/4 cup filling along each noodle, roll it up and set seam side down in the dish.
Top with the rest of the sauce and 1/2 cup mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day. Add about 10 minutes covered and check for 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled, unbaked roll-ups, wrapped well, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge overnight and bake until 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat covered until 165°F; one or two roll-ups pack well for lunch.

recipes.kids: Kids can spread the filling and roll the noodles. Spinach works in place of the chard.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles and cook as the package says.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add 1/2 pound browned Italian sausage (to 160°F) to the sauce for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the roll-ups; refrigerate or freeze unbaked.

recipes.name: Southern Fried Okra
recipes.summary: Bite-size okra coated in seasoned cornmeal and pan-fried until golden and crunchy.
equipment: large heavy skillet (cast iron works well)
steps: Toss the okra with the buttermilk in a bowl. Mix the cornmeal, flour, salt, pepper and cayenne in another.
Lift the okra out a handful at a time, let the extra buttermilk drip off, and toss in the cornmeal mix until coated.
Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers (about 350°F). Fry the okra in two batches, turning now and then, until golden brown and crisp, 5 to 7 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Serve hot.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the okra up to 1 day ahead. Fried okra is best fresh; leftovers keep 2 days.

freezer.text: Fried okra loses its crunch when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat on a baking sheet in a 400°F oven until crisp again.

recipes.kids: Kids can shake the okra in the coating in a zip-top bag. A grown-up does the frying.

swaps.gluten_free: Use all cornmeal or a gluten-free flour blend instead of the flour.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 1/2 cup plant milk with 1 1/2 teaspoons lemon juice instead of buttermilk.

prep_day.ahead: Trim and slice the okra.

recipes.name: Okra, Corn and Tomatoes
recipes.summary: A Southern summer skillet of okra, sweet corn and tomatoes with a little smoky paprika.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper 5 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the okra and cook 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomatoes with their juice, corn, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered 12 to 15 minutes, until the okra is tender.
Taste for salt and serve, over rice if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon over rice or grits, or stir into a pot of soup.

recipes.kids: The tomatoes keep okra from feeling slippery. Kids can measure the corn.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; cook 3 strips of chopped bacon first and use the fat in place of the oil for a meat version.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the okra and chop the onion and pepper.

recipes.name: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
recipes.summary: A Louisiana-style stew built on a dark roux, with chicken thighs, smoked sausage and okra, served over rice.
recipes.serving_size: about 1 1/2 cups gumbo and 1/2 cup rice
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, until the roux is the color of peanut butter or darker, 20 to 30 minutes. Lower the heat if it smokes; burned roux tastes bitter. Roux is very hot, so keep kids back from the stove.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and stir 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the broth until smooth. Add the chicken, sausage, okra, paprika, thyme, cayenne and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, 45 minutes, stirring now and then. The chicken should reach 165°F.
Meanwhile, bring the rice, water and a pinch of salt to a boil. Cover, lower the heat and simmer 18 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, taste the gumbo and add the salt if needed. Serve over the rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Gumbo is better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat to 165°F. Make the roux up to a week ahead and keep it covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze the gumbo (without rice) for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Use mild smoked sausage and leave out the cayenne; set hot sauce on the table.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend or sweet rice flour for the roux, and check the sausage label.

prep_day.ahead: Make the roux and chop the vegetables; cook the gumbo for the week.

recipes.name: Crispy Roasted Okra
recipes.summary: Whole okra pods roasted hot and fast so they turn crisp, not slippery.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the okra dry; dry okra roasts crisper.
Toss with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt on the baking sheet and spread cut side down in one layer.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes, turning once, until browned and crisp at the edges.
recipes.make_ahead: Trim the okra up to 2 days ahead. Best eaten right away.

freezer.text: Roasted okra loses its crispness when frozen.

leftovers.text: Chop into scrambled eggs or a grain bowl.

recipes.kids: Serve with ranch or ketchup for dipping, like fries.

prep_day.ahead: Trim and halve the okra.

recipes.name: Bhindi Masala (Indian Spiced Okra)
recipes.summary: Okra cooked until tender and browned with onion, tomato and warm Indian spices.

ingredients.prep: washed, dried well, sliced 1/2 inch thick

steps: Make sure the okra is completely dry before slicing; wet okra turns slippery.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the okra, stirring now and then, until browned in spots and no longer sticky, 10 to 12 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the onion and cook 5 minutes, until golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric and cayenne for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 4 minutes, until soft and saucy. Return the okra and cook 3 minutes more. Stir in the lemon juice.
Serve with naan, roti or rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a skillet to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cooked okra turns soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Roll into a warm tortilla or naan with yogurt.

recipes.kids: Skip the cayenne; the other spices are warm, not hot.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with rice instead of naan.

prep_day.ahead: Wash, dry and slice the okra.

recipes.name: Garlic Bok Choy
recipes.summary: Baby bok choy seared and steamed in a skillet with garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil in about 10 minutes.

ingredients.prep: baby bok choy, halved lengthwise and rinsed

steps: Rinse the bok choy well between the leaves, where grit hides.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Lay the bok choy cut side down and cook 2 minutes, until browned.
Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds. Add the water, cover and steam 2 to 3 minutes, until the stems are just tender.
Uncover, add the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss.
recipes.make_ahead: Rinse and halve the bok choy up to 2 days ahead. Best eaten right away.

freezer.text: Bok choy turns limp when frozen.

leftovers.text: Chop into fried rice or noodle soup.

recipes.kids: Kids can rinse the leaves and pat them dry.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.

prep_day.ahead: Rinse and halve the bok choy.

recipes.name: Ginger Chicken Noodle Soup with Bok Choy
recipes.summary: A fast, gingery chicken broth with rice noodles, bok choy and carrots.

ingredients.prep: thin rice noodles or rice sticks

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger, garlic and green onion whites 1 minute.
Add the broth and soy sauce and bring to a boil. Add the chicken breasts whole, lower the heat and simmer gently 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reads 165°F.
Lift out the chicken onto a clean board and shred or slice it.
Add the carrots and bok choy stems to the pot and simmer 3 minutes. Add the noodles and bok choy leaves and cook 3 to 5 minutes, until the noodles are tender (check the package time).
Return the chicken, stir in the sesame oil and green onion greens, and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the broth with the chicken up to 3 days ahead. Cook the noodles and bok choy when serving so they stay fresh.

freezer.text: Freeze the broth and chicken (no noodles or bok choy) for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Noodles soak up broth overnight; add more broth or water and reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can tear the bok choy leaves and help drop in the noodles. Use kitchen scissors to cut long noodles for little ones.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free and check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Use vegetable broth and cubed firm tofu instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the vegetables and cook the broth with the chicken.

recipes.name: Pork and Bok Choy Lo Mein
recipes.summary: Takeout-style noodles stir-fried with ground pork, bok choy, cabbage and carrots in a savory sauce.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling water by the package directions. Drain, rinse briefly with warm water and toss with a few drops of the sesame oil.
Stir the soy sauce, hoisin, the rest of the sesame oil and the brown sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains (160°F), about 7 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the carrot, cabbage and bok choy stems and stir-fry 3 minutes. Add the bok choy leaves and green onions for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs until everything is hot and coated, about 2 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the sauce and cut the vegetables up to 2 days ahead. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: The noodles and greens turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch and reheat to 165°F, or eat cold like a noodle salad.

recipes.kids: Kids can shake the sauce in a jar and toss the noodles with tongs once things cool a bit.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice noodles, tamari labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free hoisin.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces cubed firm tofu, browned, instead of the pork.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Chicken, Bok Choy and Snap Pea Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: Tender sliced chicken with crisp bok choy and snap peas in a honey-ginger sauce.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cornstarch and 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in one layer, turning once, until browned and 165°F inside, 5 to 6 minutes. Move to a clean plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the bok choy and snap peas and stir-fry 3 minutes, until bright green. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and cook 1 minute, until thick. Return the chicken and toss. Serve over rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Slice the chicken and keep it covered on the bottom shelf of the fridge up to 1 day. Mix the sauce up to 4 days ahead.

freezer.text: The vegetables turn limp when frozen.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch and reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Snap peas are sweet and crunchy; kids can pull off the strings.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free and check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Use pressed, cubed extra-firm tofu and vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the chicken, cut the vegetables and mix the sauce.

recipes.name: From-Scratch Green Bean Casserole
recipes.summary: Fresh green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce under a crisp, buttery Parmesan crumb topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Boil the green beans in salted water 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 7 to 8 minutes, until browned and the liquid is gone. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Season with the salt and pepper.
Stir in the beans and spread in the baking dish. Toss the panko with the melted butter and Parmesan and sprinkle on top.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until bubbling and the topping is golden.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble without the topping up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Add the topping and bake 25 to 30 minutes, until hot in the center (165°F).

freezer.text: The beans turn soft and the sauce can separate when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat covered in the oven or microwave until hot (165°F).

recipes.kids: Kids can snap the ends off the green beans and mix the crumb topping.

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch (1 1/2 tablespoons, whisked into the cold milk) and gluten-free crumbs.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil, unsweetened plant milk and skip the Parmesan.

prep_day.ahead: Blanch the beans and make the sauce; assemble and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Spring Asparagus and Radish Salad
recipes.summary: Thin ribbons of raw asparagus and sliced radishes tossed with lemon, olive oil and Parmesan.

ingredients.prep: thick spears, tough ends snapped off

steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until blended.
Lay each asparagus spear flat on a cutting board and run a vegetable peeler from the base to the tip to make long ribbons. Slice the tips that are left in thin rounds.
Toss the asparagus and radishes with the dressing and let stand 5 minutes to soften a little.
Top with the Parmesan and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Shave the asparagus and slice the radishes up to 1 day ahead; keep in a container with a damp paper towel. Dress just before serving.

freezer.text: Do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Pile onto toast with ricotta, or fold into a wrap.

recipes.kids: Older kids can make ribbons with the peeler, pushing away from their hands.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan and add toasted sunflower seeds.

prep_day.ahead: Shave the asparagus and slice the radishes.

recipes.name: Butternut Squash Mac and Cheese
recipes.summary: Creamy stovetop mac and cheese with puréed butternut squash blended into the cheddar sauce.
steps: Simmer the squash in the water in a covered saucepan 12 to 15 minutes, until very soft. Blend the squash with about 1/2 cup of its cooking water until smooth.
Meanwhile, cook the macaroni in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain.
In the empty pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer 3 minutes, stirring, until it thickens.
Lower the heat. Whisk in the squash purée, mustard, garlic powder, salt and pepper, then the cheese a handful at a time until melted.
Stir in the macaroni and heat through. Add a splash of milk if it seems thick.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook and purée the squash up to 4 days ahead, or freeze the purée. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of milk to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for up to 2 months for best quality. The sauce gets a little softer; stir in milk when reheating to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in a preheated insulated food jar for school lunch.

recipes.kids: The squash turns the sauce extra orange and a little sweet; most kids never guess it is there.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free elbows and 1 tablespoon cornstarch whisked into the cold milk instead of the flour.

prep_day.ahead: Cook and purée the squash.
